summary: Rewrote getReviewerHandoff body to match spec §5.3 5-step structure.
Step 1 (re-engagement): kept as-is — already correct (uses resolvePrerequisite dynamically).
Step 2 (FAIL → READY_FOR_DEVELOPER): replaced wpsWithQa-based FAIL branch with direct isMostRecentPipelineFail filter on non-terminal, non-blocked reviewWps.

Step 3 (PASS → next stage): replaced hard-coded wpsNotYetQaPassed/allReviewPassed logic with partitionWpsAwaitingNextStage(wpsPassedReview, 'code-review') using resolveNextAgent for dynamic routing to Release Engineer or Documentation.
Step 4 (assigned_to check): kept IN_PROGRESS branch, corrected to check assigned_to === 'Reviewer' across all wpDetails.
Step 5 (fallthrough): changed from READY_FOR_DOCUMENTATION to WAIT.

Removed: wpsWithQa (hard-coded qa:PASS gate), wpsNeedingNewReview (auto-engagement without assigned_to check), wpsWithReviewInProgress (any-IN_PROGRESS branch), wpsNotYetQaPassed (not-yet-reached-stage branch), allReviewPassed / multi-block routing logic.
Removed void partitionWpsAwaitingNextStage suppression (helper now consumed by getReviewerHandoff).
Updated 2 tests encoding removed behavior; updated test names to explain spec version.
Build: npm run build → clean (0 errors). Tests: 1872/1872 pass.

comments.note: workflow-handoff.ts: The mixed-routing fallback in getReviewerHandoff (Step 3) duplicates the Set-based nextAgents resolution already inside partitionWpsAwaitingNextStage. This could be collapsed into a single path if partitionWpsAwaitingNextStage returned the nextAgents Set directly. Deferred to a future cleanup pass.

workflow-handoff.ts: The WAIT branch for 'mixed-routing across ready WPs' in getReviewerHandoff (and analogous callers in WP-004/005) could benefit from a shared helper to keep the fallback message consistent across Reviewer / QA / Security Auditor. Low priority since it's currently duplicated across only 3 call sites.

workflow-handoff.ts: The re-engagement loop comment in getReviewerHandoff still says 'MUST precede FAIL short-circuit' without explaining the null-prerequisite skip (§21.66). The null guard is in the code but the comment doesn't mention it — a future reader might miss why the loop can exit without firing. Suggest adding a one-liner: '// resolvePrerequisite returns null → code-review is first active stage → re-engagement skip is intentional (§21.66)'.

AC2 PASS: The only IN_PROGRESS return paths for Reviewer are (a) the re-engagement guard (spec-defined, Step 1) and (b) Step 4 which gates strictly on wp.assigned_to === 'Reviewer'. The old any-IN_PROGRESS bug is confirmed removed.
AC3 PASS: resolvePrerequisite('code-review', reviewActiveStages) is used in Step 1 for dynamic upstream resolution — no 'qa' hard-code appears anywhere in getReviewerHandoff.
AC4 PASS: npm run build → tsc clean, 0 errors.
Full suite: 62 test files, 1872/1872 pass, vitest exit 0. Previously observed exit code 1 was a PowerShell Select-Object pipeline artifact, not a real failure.

comments.note: No security findings — all OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed; no Critical or High issues identified. The rewrite aligns getReviewerHandoff with spec §5.3 (5-step structure). Template literals interpolate schema-validated ledger IDs and constant-derived role names only — no user-controlled string reaches any interpreter. The ready[0]! non-null assertion is safe (gated by ready.length > 0). Dynamic routing via resolvePrerequisite/resolveNextAgent returns enum-typed constants, not user input.

summary: Code review PASS with 2 Fix-Forward edits. getReviewerHandoff correctly implements spec §5.3 5-step structure with dynamic upstream resolution, no hard-coded qa:PASS gate, and proper FAIL/re-engagement/assigned_to routing. Fix-Forward 1: removed dead ternary branch in Step 3 (ready.length > 0 guard already ensured it). Fix-Forward 2: added null-prerequisite skip explanation to Step 1 comment (§21.66 case), resolving the Developer's debt note. All 8 ACs met.

comments.note: Removed dead ternary in Step 3 (workflow-handoff.ts getReviewerHandoff). `const nextAgentName = ready.length > 0 ? resolveNextAgent(...) : 'next stage'` was inside `if (ready.length > 0)`, making the `'next stage'` branch unreachable. Simplified to direct `resolveNextAgent(...)` call. Non-behavioral — the ready[0]! non-null assertion was already safe due to the outer guard.

Resolved Developer debt note: added null-prerequisite skip explanation to Step 1 comment (workflow-handoff.ts getReviewerHandoff). Added: 'resolvePrerequisite returns null → code-review is the first active stage → re-engagement skip is intentional (§21.66): no upstream stage exists to have re-passed.' This makes explicit why the loop can exit without firing for documentation-only or first-stage WPs. Non-behavioral comment addition.

The 5-step structure of getReviewerHandoff is clean. Dynamic routing via partitionWpsAwaitingNextStage/resolveNextAgent correctly handles the Release Engineer → Documentation path variation without any hard-coded stage names. The mixed-routing fallback (WAIT with agent list) is a good defensive pattern.

Step 4 of getReviewerHandoff (assigned_to === 'Reviewer' → IN_PROGRESS) lacks a dedicated unit test. Flagged by QA; confirming here. Suggest adding: `makeWp('WP-001','IN_PROGRESS', [{type:'implementation',status:'PASS'}], [], 'Reviewer')` → expect IN_PROGRESS with current_agent==='Reviewer'.
